chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Exchange gifts, you will find affection. Exchange gifts, for indeed it removes malice.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of exchanging gifts in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith links the physical act of giving (tahadhu) directly to the emotional state of love (tahabbu), a concept central to Shia ethics where material exchange serves as a vehicle for spiritual and social cohesion. Scholars note that 'dagha'in' refers not just to minor annoyances but to deep-seated resentments, making this practice a proactive mechanism for maintaining communal harmony (usul al-mu'amalat).
